title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1-12
content:
## Introduction
During the first trimester of pregnancy, nutrition plays a crucial role in the development of the fetus. Prioritizing essential nutrients and safe foods will help ensure the health and well-being of both the mother and the fetus.

## Folic Acid - A Crucial Nutrient
Folic acid is one of the most important nutrients during the first trimester of pregnancy. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), folic acid helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. Pregnant women should consume 400-800 micrograms of folic acid per day. Foods rich in folic acid include leafy greens, fruits, and dairy products.

## Iron - An Essential Nutrient
Iron is another essential nutrient during the first trimester of pregnancy. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), iron helps prevent anemia in pregnant women. Pregnant women should consume 27 milligrams of iron per day. Foods rich in iron include red meat, poultry, fish, and legumes.

## Safe Foods
During the first trimester of pregnancy, pregnant women should prioritize safe foods to avoid bacterial and viral infections. According to the National Health Service (NHS), pregnant women should avoid foods like sushi, sashimi, and undercooked meat. Instead, they should choose cooked foods like beef, chicken, and fish.

## Hydration - A Crucial Aspect
Hydration is also crucial during the first trimester of pregnancy. According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), water helps prevent dehydration and other health problems. Pregnant women should drink at least 8 glasses of water per day.

## Conclusion
During the first trimester of pregnancy, pregnant women should prioritize essential nutrients and safe foods to ensure the health and well-being of both the mother and the fetus. faqs.question: Why is folic acid important during the first trimester of pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Folic acid helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus.

faqs.question: How can pregnant women ensure they are getting enough iron in their diet?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women should consume 27 milligrams of iron per day from iron-rich foods like red meat, poultry, fish, and legumes.

faqs.question: Why should pregnant women avoid foods like sushi and sashimi?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women should avoid foods like sushi and sashimi because they can contain harmful bacteria and viruses that can affect the health of the mother and the fetus.
